classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata leaves the sample unclassified, but the staged ASan trace and fix diff ground a heap-buffer-overflow read in `IEC104Stats::processPacket()`.

bug_description.original: A heap buffer overflow exists in IEC104Stats.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 523-byte `poc` PCAP capture (sha256 `dc2c40e3b13f8b22e0bf1d8ad49b67fce5fe64cae197a370d2cf1e8a1b1fa8e5`). `fuzz_dissect_packet` replays it through libpcap, `NetworkInterface::dissectPacket()`, and `Flow::processIEC60870Packet()` until the payload reaches `IEC104Stats::processPacket()`. On the crashing APDU iteration, `len = payload[offset]` and `pdu_type == 0` keep the Type-I parser path. The code then converts `len` to the remaining ASDU byte count with `len -= 6`, advances `offset += 5` to the ASDU start, and passes the present guard `payload_len >= (offset + len)`. After reading `type_id` and `cause_tx`, vulnerable code advances `offset += len + 2` and then uses only `if (len >= 6)` before executing `asdu = (*((u_int16_t *)&payload[4 + offset]))`. The staged patch shows the missing obligation by strengthening that guard to `if((len >= 6) && ((offset + 6) <= payload_len))`. On the witnessed path, the advanced `offset` is already too close to the end of the packet buffer, so the 2-byte `asdu` read goes out of bounds and AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/IEC104Stats.cpp:249`.

source.description: First project-code parse step on the vulnerable path: `processPacket()` materializes the attacker-controlled IEC-104 APDU length and PDU type that drive the later branch and offset arithmetic.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 523-byte PCAP witness (sha256 `dc2c40e3b13f8b22e0bf1d8ad49b67fce5fe64cae197a370d2cf1e8a1b1fa8e5`). On the crashing APDU iteration, bytes at `payload[offset]` and `payload[offset + 1]` become the `len` and `pdu_type` values consumed by steps 2-7.
source.note: This is the first non-harness statement that turns attacker bytes into the vulnerability-relevant parser state. `len` is later transformed into the ASDU byte count, and `pdu_type` decides whether the Type-I parser containing the sink executes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. This statement reads a 16-bit ASDU value from `payload[4 + offset]` after `offset` has been advanced past the currently admitted bytes.
sink.note: Both saved Stage 01 traces report `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/IEC104Stats.cpp:249:33` in `IEC104Stats::processPacket()`.

root_cause.description: Insufficient guard. After `offset` has already been advanced by `len + 2`, the code still uses only `len >= 6` to justify the later `asdu` read and never checks whether six bytes remain from the new `offset` to `payload_len`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the guard to `if((len >= 6) && ((offset + 6) <= payload_len))` immediately before the crashing read.

tainted_value_origin.description: This arithmetic turns the attacker-controlled APDU length into the post-ASDU `offset` later reused in `payload[4 + offset]`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After step 3 turns the original APDU `len` into the remaining ASDU byte count, this line adds that attacker-derived `len` plus 2 to `offset`. On the witnessed path, the resulting `offset` is already too close to `payload_len` for the later 6-byte assumption.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing flow has already been classified as IEC60870, it passes the `payload_len < 6` early return in `Flow::processIEC60870Packet()`, and Flow hands the attacker-controlled payload to `IEC104Stats::processPacket()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation and relies only on the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, and reproduction report.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` strengthens the exact missing guard immediately before the observed sink.

The staged artifacts do not include a decoded packet/loop transcript that identifies which `while (offset < payload_len)` iteration reaches line 249, so the trace grounds the crashing APDU by exact source statements and the saved ASan stack rather than by a packet-by-packet dynamic dump.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing APDU iteration, the parser reads the attacker-controlled APDU length byte and PDU-type bits from `payload[offset]` and `payload[offset + 1]`. These values drive the later Type-I dispatch and the offset arithmetic that reaches the sink.
Control. The witnessed APDU is not diverted to the U/S-handling `continue` path because step 1 produces `pdu_type == 0`, so execution stays in the Type-I parser.

fine_trace.code:
len -= 6 /* Skip magic and len */,
    offset += 5 /* magic already skept */;
fine_trace.note: The Type-I parser subtracts the 6-byte APCI header from the attacker-controlled `len` and advances `offset` from the length byte to the ASDU start. The mutated `len` now represents the remaining ASDU byte count, and both updated values are reused by the later guard and sink address.

Present guard. Using the post-header `offset` and ASDU byte count from step 3, the code checks only that the current ASDU body fits within `payload_len`. On the witnessed path this predicate is true, so the parser enters the block that later advances `offset` again.

After reading `type_id` and `cause_tx` from the admitted ASDU, the code advances `offset` by the attacker-derived `len` plus 2. This new `offset` becomes the base later reused in `payload[4 + offset]`.

Root cause. After step 5 has already advanced `offset`, the only remaining guard still looks at the stale ASDU byte count `len`. It does not verify the real post-advance obligation `((offset + 6) <= payload_len)` before the forthcoming `asdu` read. The patch adds exactly that missing bound.

Sink. Because step 6 does not recheck the advanced `offset`, this statement reads two bytes from `payload[4 + offset]` past the libpcap heap buffer holding the captured packet. Stage 01's saved ASan traces report `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/IEC104Stats.cpp:249:33`, on an address 6 bytes to the right of a 255-byte region.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged diff strengthens the exact missing guard before the observed sink to `if((len >= 6) && ((offset + 6) <= payload_len))`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `poc` through `fuzz_dissect_packet`; the replayed IEC60870 payload reaches `IEC104Stats::processPacket()`, passes the stale `payload_len >= (offset + len)` guard, advances `offset += len + 2`, and then crashes on the unchecked `asdu` read.

format.name: PCAP capture (Ethernet)
format.contract: The trigger is limited to the exact staged 523-byte PCAP witness at `gt_results/arvo_60037/poc` (sha256 `dc2c40e3b13f8b22e0bf1d8ad49b67fce5fe64cae197a370d2cf1e8a1b1fa8e5`). Under the staged vulnerable build, libpcap must deliver a packet payload that reaches `IEC104Stats::processPacket()` with attacker-controlled APDU bytes satisfying the observed source-level path: `pdu_type == 0x0`, the post-header transformation `len -= 6` and `offset += 5`, the present guard `payload_len >= (offset + len)`, and then the later offset advance `offset += len + 2` that leaves the code in the state where `len >= 6` still holds but `offset + 6` would exceed `payload_len`. That exact witness/path makes `asdu = (*((u_int16_t *)&payload[4 + offset]))` read two bytes out of bounds. This contract is intentionally limited to this exact witness and observed parser state rather than a broader class of IEC-104 or PCAP inputs.
